neighbours.label: The first piece W or F of a romanized Chinese place name (W|uhan, W|uxi, F|oshan, F|uzhou); W and F names elsewhere stay quiet
fire: The high-speed line runs from Nanjing through Wuhu and Fuyang.
Factories in Dongguan and Foshan have raised their wages.
She flew from Chengdu to Wuxi for the trade fair.
Tea from Fujian and Wuyi is sold across the province.
Trains leave Suzhou and Wuxi every twenty minutes.
Our supplier moved its plant from Xiamen to Fuzhou.
Tourists often combine Hangzhou with Wuzhen and Wenzhou.
The river floods towns near Fuling and Wanzhou each year.
quiet: The high-speed line runs from Lyon through Avignon and Marseille.
Factories in Detroit and Flint have raised their wages.
She flew from Boston to Warsaw for the trade fair.
Tea from Florida and Wales is sold across the country.
Trains leave Vienna and Frankfurt every twenty minutes.
Our supplier moved its plant from Dallas to Fresno.
Tourists often combine Prague with Wroclaw and Weimar.
The river floods towns near Worms and Freiburg each year.

notes: Whole-token pinyin surnames (Fang 0.05) and sentence-initial citations did not fire in probes, so the label is limited to split place names.
